title: BTC exposure. A clearer way to reduce risk.
body: An owner-controlled account borrows MUSD against BTC and routes through Mezo Pools. Permissionless guards can reduce risk within the owner's settings.
guide: Start with the product: BTC holders choose exposure; the account holds the trove. This is an illustrative walkthrough, not a new transaction recording.

title: 01  Review, then open.
body: Choose BTC size and collateral ratio. Review gross MUSD minted, the separate Coil fee, depth, caps and pause state before signing.
cards: Default Coil fee on new mint
guide: The transaction enforces the accepted fee ceiling. A flash open succeeds atomically only when pool liquidity, oracle bounds and opening policy allow it.

title: 02  Fund a guard. Keep ownership.
body: Set a guard floor and target, park MUSD and fund MEZO tips. Anyone may trigger permitted risk reduction; the caller cannot take BTC or MUSD.
guide: A guard is a best-effort risk tool, not guaranteed liquidation protection. With an empty reserve and unsafe sale, it returns false without a tip.

title: 03  Repay, claim, or close.
body: Approve MUSD to the account for safe repayment. Claim only recovered surplus. Close with funded MUSD only when Mezo permits the protocol close.
cards: Safe pure repayment in Recovery Mode
guide: Recovery Mode blocks new leverage and can block full close. It does not imply a guaranteed exit. Rescue, repayment, claim and exit carry zero Coil fee.

title: One bound. Explicit operational limits.
body: All pool fills use the same PriceMin snapshot before flash and in callback, including owner flash close. No second slippage widening.
cards: Repay, guard and top-up stay available
guide: Public keeper status must show scan freshness and execution mode. A process start, old heartbeat or monitoring-only service is not active transaction protection.

title: Historical execution is useful evidence.
body: An October testnet run recorded flash open, a ratio-improving guard with a 1 MEZO tip, and close. Those receipts belong to an older factory.
guide: Historical receipts do not prove the completion release's fees, claim or Recovery Mode flow. Exact links and limitations are in DEPLOYMENTS.md.

title: A release earns its proof.
body: The new build still needs funded matsnet feature receipts, full indexed source verification, matching app and keeper metadata, and 3-5 recruited testers.
guide: Existing clones are not upgradeable. Mainnet stays gated, starts paused and requires a separate go-live decision after the release checks pass. The contracts are unaudited.
